title: As Driven control archetype registry
description: Named bundles of transmission control values that many cars share. An archetype is descriptive: it never supplies a value to a record, and a record always keeps its own resolved controls. See docs/archetypes.md.

archetype_id.description: Stable key naming the mechanism, never a racing class. Class predicts controls badly enough that the dataset disproves it: the nine curated GT4 cars split on both forward gears and standing-start clutch, and the largest single mechanism spans CART, GT1, IndyCar and GTR entries. Name what the driver does, as in sequential-stick-6-clutch-start-blip-down.

label.description: Short human phrase for review output and curation notes. Not shown to drivers; the preflight card keeps rendering resolved values.

transmission.description: The complete transmission block this archetype stands for, in the same shape as a car record's authentic_controls.transmission. Its structure is enforced against the car record schema's $defs/transmission during validation rather than being restated here, so the two cannot drift. An archetype must be fully specified: no member field may be unknown, because an archetype that is itself uncertain cannot describe anything.

basis.description: Why this archetype exists as a distinct mechanism, and what separates it from its nearest neighbour. A reviewer should be able to tell from this line alone whether a given car belongs.
